title: Quebec teenager celebrates Ella's victory at World Dairy Expo
summary:
A Canadian teenager and her favourite cow earned a major honour at the World Dairy Expo in Madison, Wisconsin, on Sunday. Alyson Doiron, a 16-year-old high school student from Cap-Santé, Quebec, celebrated when Ella won the top prize at the International Junior Holstein Show.

The five-year-old cow's full name is Arolene Dempsey Ella. Holstein refers to a breed of dairy cattle, the cows kept for milk production. At a cattle show, animals enter an arena to be judged in a competition.

Doiron cheered and cried as she received Ella's award. She described Ella as easy to work with and much loved. For Doiron, the result also demonstrated the strength of cow showing in her home province.

These contests can have consequences beyond a trophy. A major victory can increase an animal's value by tens of thousands of dollars, and its future offspring may become more valuable too.

Although the Expo attracts an international gathering, health and safety regulations limit its animal competitions to cows from Canadian and American farms. Canadian, American and Mexican flags hang above the judging arena.

Transporting cows to the event requires considerable effort. Brian Carscadden, the executive senior manager and part owner of Quebec dairy company Blondin Sires, said his team travelled more than 1,500 kilometres from St. Placide to Madison, bringing 25 cows in trailers.

The gathering happened against the background of a trade dispute between Canada and the United States. Carscadden said his business had not yet been affected and that the dispute rarely came up in conversations at the Expo. Some American visitors expressed frustration about trade policies and living costs.

The event brought Canadian and American farms together for competition, with Doiron and Ella celebrating their success.
why_it_matters: Ella's win shows how farming competitions can matter to young participants and influence the value of animals and their offspring.
